correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all quantifiers and field/ring hypotheses. Fitting decomposition proves N_r=q^{r²-r}; fixed-rank matrix normal form gives conditional nilpotency probability q^{-r}; a uniform random vector has vanishing probability q^{-r} for a fixed rank-r map; its m-step survival probability is (1-q^{-n})^m. Wedderburn–Artin and coordinate independence yield the finite semisimple product. Weighted exhaustive product counts over F2 dimensions 1,2,3 and F3 dimension 2 at lengths through 4 reproduce the exact formulas. The checker uses actual nth matrix powers, not the proof identity.

originality.rationale: Compared exact statements and implications with the full 10-page motivating preprint, the complete 5-page nilpotent-matrix census proof, the full texts of two closest published finite-matrix findings, and multiple targeted published-finding and scholarly searches. No inspected source states or entails the all-length unrestricted full-matrix law. Coinciding field probabilities do not imply ring-level equality, and constrained factorization and triangular-subring results do not cover it. Residual risk of unindexed literature is explicitly recognized; searches alone do not establish universal uniqueness.
residual_risks: The exact formula could be implicit in unindexed earlier random finite-matrix-product studies or inaccessible enumeration tables; neither failed nor successful searches alone prove uniqueness.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 NPP paper resolves commutative and special triangular situations but gives no exact probability on full matrix algebras. The new law settles that natural noncommutative class in every dimension and for every product length; its unexpected equality with zero-product probability over an extension field is a structural collapse not visible from a single nilpotent count. The semisimple formula completes the invariant for every finite semisimple ring. This is a motivated exact classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or a renaming of field arithmetic.
